# manygit

> A single CLI tool to manage multiple git repositories: a lazygit-style terminal
> UI for a whole tree of git repos. Point it at a directory and it shows every git
> repository nested under it on one screen — which are ahead, behind, or dirty —
> then fetches, pulls, pushes, and switches branches on the one under the cursor,
> without cd-ing between them.

manygit is a single Go binary for macOS, Linux and Windows, built with Bubble
Tea and Lip Gloss. It is free and open source at
https://github.com/rabeeh-ta/manygit

## What problem it solves

If you keep more than a handful of git repos in one tree — microservices, a
workspace of packages, a folder of plugins, nested at whatever depth — answering
"which of these have uncommitted work, and which are behind origin?" means
`cd`-ing through every one, or maintaining a shell loop like:

    for d in */; do (cd "$d" && git status); done

manygit replaces that loop with a screen you can act from. It is to a folder of
repos what lazygit is to a single repo.

## How it compares to other multi-repo tools

Most tools in this space — `gita`, `mani`, `mu-repo`, `meta`, `myrepos` — are
batch command runners: you register repos in a config file, broadcast a git or
shell command to all of them, and read the printed output. They are good at
running one command across many repos.

manygit is the interactive counterpart. There is no config file to maintain: it
discovers repos by walking the directory, keeps their status live on screen, and
you act on one repo at a time from the list without leaving it. Pick a batch
runner to script across repos; pick manygit to *look* at them and work.

Compared to `lazygit`, which manygit is modelled on: lazygit is a TUI for one
repository, manygit is a TUI for the folder containing many.

## Install

macOS, via Homebrew:

    brew tap rabeeh-ta/manygit
    brew trust rabeeh-ta/manygit
    brew install manygit

The trust step is required from Homebrew 6 onwards: casks in a third-party tap can
run arbitrary Ruby, so Homebrew refuses to load them until the tap is trusted.
`brew trust --cask rabeeh-ta/manygit/manygit` trusts only manygit instead of the
whole tap.

macOS and Linux, via the installer script:

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rabeeh-ta/manygit/main/install.sh | bash

Windows, via PowerShell:

    irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rabeeh-ta/manygit/main/install.ps1 | iex

(Git Bash, MSYS2, Cygwin and WSL can use install.sh instead — it detects Windows
there too and installs the same binary.)

The installer-script build self-updates: it offers to replace itself when a newer
release exists. A Homebrew or `go install` build is owned by that package manager,
so manygit never replaces it — it reports the new release at most once a day, after
you quit, and names the command that installs it.

With Go (needs Go 1.24+):

    go install github.com/rabeeh-ta/manygit@latest

From source:

    git clone https://github.com/rabeeh-ta/manygit && cd manygit
    go build -o ~/.local/bin/manygit .

## Usage

    manygit                 # scan the current directory
    manygit --root ~/work   # scan a specific folder

It walks the folder three levels deep by default, skips `node_modules`, `vendor`,
`dist`, `target` and similar, and groups the repos it finds by parent directory.

## Panes

- `1` Repos — every repo, its current branch, and its status
- `2` Scripts — script files near the root, runnable in place (`*.sh`
  everywhere; `*.ps1`, `*.cmd`, `*.bat` also count on Windows)
- `3` Branches — the highlighted repo's local and remote branches
- `4` PRs — GitHub pull requests (needs the `gh` CLI, signed in)
- `5` Graph — a colored commit graph for the highlighted repo
- `6` Changes — changed files of the selected commit, with in-place diffs
- `7` Output — live output of the last script run

## Keys

Actions apply to the repo under the `>` cursor.

- `j` / `k` — move within the focused pane
- `←` / `→` — hop between Repos and that repo's Branches
- `enter` — open a repo's branches, check one out, run a script, or check out a PR
- `s` / `p` — sync (fetch then fast-forward pull) / push
- `d` / `D` — discard changes after a confirm (`D` also deletes untracked files)
- `f` / `r` — fetch this repo / refetch all
- `/` — filter the focused list; Repos match on name AND current branch (and the
  tag while `t` is on)
- `F` — show only repos that are changed, ahead, or behind
- `t` — show each repo's latest tag inline
- `g` / `n` — full-screen commit graph / full-screen news feed
- `m` — in the PRs pane, toggle your PRs and review requests
- `:` — plain-English git: the request goes to your AI harness (claude or codex) with the
  repo tree as context; it replies with git commands, manygit shows them and runs them only
  after you confirm. Only git — never a shell, never a force-push or a remote delete.
  Reference a file with `@path` (tab-completes on the scripts it found) to send its
  contents along: `@scripts/update-all.sh only the frontend apps from this`. Referenced
  files must live inside the scanned tree.
- `!` — shell in the highlighted repo. Opens a prompt reading `$manygit:apps/api-gateway`
  (the key is `!`, vim's shell-escape convention; the prompt itself renders as a shell
  prompt naming where you are — the repo's path relative to the scanned root, shortened
  from the left with `…` on a narrow terminal). Type a bash command and it runs there
  (falling back to `cmd.exe` on Windows if bash isn't on PATH), with its
  combined stdout and stderr streaming into the Output pane. The prompt stays open after
  each command, so it is a shell you sit in rather than a one-shot. The bottom bar shows
  the repo name while you type, so it is always clear which folder the command lands in.
  `esc` leaves the shell and returns focus to the Repos pane; it does NOT stop a running
  command — `ctrl+c` does that. `up`/`down` recall this session's earlier commands. No
  confirm and no blocklist — it is a shell escape and runs exactly what you typed, with
  the command echoed into the pane as the record. Non-interactive (no TTY), so `vim`,
  `top` and `sudo` prompts do not work.
- `o` / `z` — open the repo in your editor / zoom the focused pane
- `tab` / `shift+tab` — cycle the panes
- `[` / `]` — cycle the focused pane's tabs
- `esc` — back out one layer of state (diff, then Changes, zoom, then the filters)
- `?` — help: a full-screen overlay with two faces, the keybindings and the status
  legend on one, settings (theme, AI harness, news window, scan depth, glyphs,
  editor) on the other. `tab` / `shift+tab` / `[` / `]` switch faces; `?` or `esc`
  closes from either. Settings has no key of its own.
- `q` — quit
- `esc esc` — quit with two consecutive presses within 500 ms, from any screen; any other key resets the sequence

## Status column

- `ok` — up to date with upstream
- `↑N` — N commits ahead, something to push
- `↓N` — N commits behind, something to pull
- `↑N ↓M` — diverged
- `*N` — N files changed in the working tree
- `no-remote` — a local-only repo, never pushed anywhere
- `!` — the branch has no upstream, or git errored

## Other features

- Plain-English git (`:`): type a request, your AI harness turns it into git
  commands against the whole tree, you confirm them, manygit runs them. `@path`
  sends a file along as context. Only git, never a shell; force-pushes and remote
  deletions are refused; a batch stops at the first failure. Each request stands
  alone — there is no conversation, so it never asks a question: it picks the most
  likely reading and you approve or decline the commands.
- GitHub PRs: with the `gh` CLI signed in, `4` lists your open PRs and the ones
  awaiting your review. It opens on whichever of the two has something in it —
  yours normally, review requests when yours are empty and reviews are waiting;
  picking a list with `m` then sticks. Each PR takes two lines: number, author
  and title, then the repo, the branch that clone is currently on, and
  `base ← head` — what merges into what. `enter` checks the PR's branch out in
  the matching local clone via `gh pr checkout`, and leaves the focus, the PR
  cursor and the repo cursor exactly where they were, because a PR usually spans
  several repos.
- Live repo state: the Repos pane follows what happens to the repos rather than
  waiting to be refreshed. Checking out a PR updates that repo's row in place,
  and while a script or a `:` plan is running manygit re-reads the repos it
  touches as it touches them, then re-reads all of them once when the run ends.
  The Output pane has one owner at a time: starting a script supersedes a pending
  `:` reply and vice versa, so neither can write into the other's output.
- AI news feed: with `claude` or `codex` on PATH, the top bar summarizes recent
  commits across every repo in English. Cached four hours.
- Themes: `default`, `serika_dark`, `dracula`, `nord`, `catppuccin`, `8008`,
  adapted from monkeytype. Configurable in `~/.config/manygit/config.yml` or the
  settings face of the `?` overlay.

## Safety

manygit never writes to the folder you launch it from. On its own it never
force-pushes, merges, or rebases: `s` is fetch + fast-forward-only pull, and `p`
is a plain push. The only destructive action it offers on its own is discarding a
repo's changes (`d` / `D`), which always asks first.

`!` is the deliberate exception: it runs the bash command you type in the
highlighted repo (falling back to `cmd.exe` on Windows if bash isn't on PATH),
with no confirm and no blocklist, because a shell escape that second-guessed
you would be useless. The command is echoed into the Output pane with the repo
it ran in, so there is a record, and `ctrl+c` stops it mid-run.

`:` widens that, deliberately. It can merge, rebase, tag and push, because that
is what it is for — but only commands it has shown you and you have confirmed,
and it runs `git` with an argument list rather than through a shell, so pipes and
`&&` are not expressible. Force-pushes, remote deletions, and the git flags that
take a shell command (`-c`, `rebase --exec`, `submodule foreach`, `filter-branch`,
`bisect run`) are refused before the confirm ever appears.
